To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
increased expression of transforming-growth factor-beta 1 in human tumor cells results in increased glycolysis, adhesiveness, integrin and plasmogen activator synthesis, and tumorigenicity.

(a) overexpression of TGF-beta 2 in 293 cells results in increased metabolic rate, increased adhesiveness and increased tumorigenic capacity; (b) these effects occur in cells expressing either latent or active TFG-beta, indicating that some level of latent TGF- beta is sufficient to induce these changes, and (c) overexpression of active TGF- beta, but not latent, results in increased tumorigenic potential.
overexpression of TGF-beta 2 in tumor cells results in increased glycolysis, enhanced adhesiveness, increased expression of several beta 3 integrins, and increased tumorigenic capacity.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the role of the transforming growth factor beta in the regulation of cell adhesion, proliferation and differentiation, and in particular with the mechanisms involved in the activation and release of latent TGF beta 1.
the physiological effects of TGF-β overexpression on tumor cells.
the physiological effects of overexpressing Tgf-beta1 in tumor cells, and with the possible role of this cytokine in tumor progression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expression of active TGF- beta in a tumor cell line can lead to a phenotype that is more favorable for tumor growth.
increased TGF-beta expression results in a more aggressive phenotype.
TGF-beta 3 overproduction by tumor cells results in a more aggressive phenotype.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

increased expression of TGB-beta 1 in 293 cells induces several phenotypic changes, including increased metabolic activity, adhesiveness, and tumorigenicity, all of which may play an important role in tumor development and progression.
increased expression of TFG-beta1 in a tumor cell can lead to increased tumor formation and growth.

increased expression of TFG-beta 1, in the absence of direct growth inhibitory effects on the tumor cells themselves, is associated with increased glycolysis and enhanced tumorigenicity, and that this phenotype is induced by both latent and active TGF-beta 2.
The main takeaway from our work is that
increased TGF-beta production by tumor cells may have a significant impact on tumor growth and progression, even when the tumor cells themselves are not growth inhibited by TGF-beta.
TGF-beta is not only a potent tumor suppressor but also a potent tumor promoter.
TGF beta 1 can be an oncogene.
